extracted.intended_audience: Gavi-supported countries and programmes; country health ministries, programme managers, and donor/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A catalogue of Gavi's programmatic and related corporate policies that set principles, requirements and procedures governing Gavi support to countries (eligibility, funding, risk, accountability, health systems, etc.). Useful for countries and programme teams preparing requests for Gavi support or implementing Gavi-funded activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic policies (overarching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gavi’s programmatic policies set out principles for Gavi-supported countries and programmes. Approved by the Gavi Board and reviewed on a regular basis, these policies aim to ensure that Gavi support is efficient, transparent, and fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policies provide the guiding principles that all specific programmatic policies implement; they are Board-approved and periodically reviewed to ensure efficiency, transparency and fairness in Gavi support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework for Gavi Funding to Countries
rubrics_metrics.description: An overarching document that outlines the key objectives and principles under which Gavi provides funding to eligible countries and describes the interactions between the three funding policies: Eligibility and Transition, Co-financing, and Health Systems and Immunisation Strengthening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places the three funding policies in context of other Gavi support and initiatives not covered in the policies (e.g., the Middle-Income Country Approach); used to interpret how funding policies interact and apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate policies (overarching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gavi’s corporate policies ensure efficiency, transparency and accountability in our corporate processes and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate policies complement programmatic policies by governing internal processes and accountability mechanisms that affect how programme support is delivered and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑financing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Co‑financing means that countries contribute to the cost of Gavi-supported vaccines by financing some of the required vaccine doses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations and rules for the level and form of country contribution toward vaccine costs when Gavi provides support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for Gavi support is determined by countries' national income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the criteria and thresholds (based on national income) that determine which countries qualify for Gavi assistance and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fragility, emergencies and displaced populations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Gavi enables flexible and tailored support through bespoke and differentiated interventions in countries facing chronic fragility; agile and coordinated response in acute emergencies; and a laser focus on displaced populations in Gavi-eligible…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides differentiated, flexible and context-specific programming for fragile contexts, acute emergencies and displaced populations to ensure appropriate and timely Gavi support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender equality is a fundamental human right and a powerful driver for better health outcomes globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames Gavi programming to consider and promote gender equality as an objective and driver of improved immunisation and health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health system and immunisation strengthening (HSIS) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy that guides Gavi’s support to health system and immunisation strengthening (HSIS). The purpose of the HSIS policy, in effect from January 2023, is to set out the principles, general requirements and procedures for Gavi’s HSIS…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies principles, general requirements and procedures for Gavi support to health systems and immunisation strengthening activities; informs how HSIS funding is designed, approved and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritisation mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: When overall demand for support from Gavi-eligible countries is higher than available donor resources, the Vaccine Alliance must make fair, transparent and objective decisions on how to use its available resources most effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the principles and process for allocating scarce resources across competing country requests to ensure fairness, transparency and effectiveness in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk policy forms the overarching framework for Gavi’s risk management approach. It is embedded in various structures and processes for risk monitoring, reporting and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines the framework for identifying, monitoring, reporting and mitigating risks across Gavi programmes and operations; integrates risk considerations into decision-making and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑procurement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuring quality vaccines and immunisation products for countries that procure their own products with Gavi funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets requirements and assurance mechanisms to ensure quality, safety and appropriate procurement practices where countries use Gavi funding to procure vaccines themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gavi is to deliver on its mission, it must take some risk, and do everything possible to mitigate that risk. Donors realise this, but also rightly expect risks to be minimised and action to be taken when misuse is uncovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines expectations and mechanisms for transparency, risk mitigation and taking action in cases of misuse; underpins donor confidence through accountability measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine donation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Donations of vaccines by industry to international organisations or to governments can bring benefits if properly managed, but also carry certain risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides principles and safeguards for managing vaccine donations to maximize benefits and mitigate risks associated with donated products.
